cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Lose Something for Me
cards.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Will you give me your first turn, even if it costs you the match?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. You said you were on my side. This side has a cost.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lend the emotion a turn so I can see it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Will you give me your first turn, even if it costs you the match?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. You said you were on my side. This side has a cost.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lend the emotion a turn so I can see it.

mechanism: A judges whether B loyalty counts by requiring a concrete sacrifice for A benefit, deciding that convenient or purely emotional support is insufficient.
confusable: D202 asks priorities among values; D203 deliberately makes B loss the evidence of allegiance to A.
comparison: Game turn gives A a competitive edge at B cost; opening-night attendance costs B receiving an earned prize.
seedUse: Both cards and all four canonical seeds read. Preserve a real disadvantage and sincere need for loyalty, without presenting A test as objectively fair.
